word-order.focus: the order the words come in
facts: Every row keeps the same order of roles. Copy the order the rows use, not the order English uses.
word-order.offline1: Same words, but the rows put them in another order. Compare the rows.

facts: In these rows the action word can wait until the end of its clause.
verb-final.offline1: Where does the action word sit in the rows?

particles.focus: the small tag words after each thing
facts: Small tag words follow a noun and say what job it does: who acts, and what is acted on.
particles.offline1: Every noun wears a little tag. Which tag marks who does it?

compound-meaning.focus: how longer words are built from smaller parts
facts: Some words are built from smaller meaningful parts, joined in a fixed order.
compound-meaning.offline1: Build the word from the meanings of its parts, in the order the rows use.

adjective-order.focus: whether a describing word comes before or after its thing
facts: Most describing words here come after the thing they describe.
adjective-order.offline1: In the rows, which comes first: the thing, or what it is like?

gender-agreement.focus: the little words around each thing
facts: Every noun has a grammatical gender, and the little words around it change to match.
gender-agreement.offline1: The words around a noun must match its gender.

plural-agreement.focus: how the rows show that there are many
facts: When there is more than one, the plural shows on more than one word of the phrase.
plural-agreement.offline1: When there are many, every word in the phrase shows it.

verb-ending.focus: the endings of the action words
facts: The ending of the action word shows who is doing it.
verb-ending.offline1: Here the end of the action word says who is acting.

punctuation.focus: the marks at both ends of the sentences
facts: A question or an exclamation is marked at its start as well as its end.
punctuation.offline1: The phrase is missing its marks. Look at both ends of the rows.

suffix-order.focus: the order of the endings stacked on a word
facts: Endings stack onto a word in a fixed order, one meaning per ending.
suffix-order.offline1: Right pieces, wrong train. The endings always couple in the same order.

facts: The vowel in an ending changes to match the vowels of the word it joins.
vowel-harmony.offline1: The endings clash. Their vowels must match the vowels of the word they join.

measure-word.focus: the word between this or that and the thing
facts: A pointed-at or counted thing takes a measure word that fits its kind, just before the thing.
measure-word.offline1: A counted thing needs the shape-word that fits it.

consonant-root.focus: the consonants that related words share
facts: Related words share a skeleton of consonants that carries the core meaning.
consonant-root.offline1: The skeleton is wrong. The meaning lives in the shared consonants.

vowel-pattern.focus: the vowels set around the shared consonants
facts: The pattern of vowels around a consonant skeleton says what role the word plays.
vowel-pattern.offline1: Right bones, wrong flesh. The vowel pattern says what role the word plays.

vocabulary.focus: which word goes with which picture
facts: Each word keeps its meaning from row to row. Match words to the meanings they appear with.
vocabulary.offline1: That word means something else here. Check the meanings again.
